thread:
incident-bot: ALERT P1 1: potential KV cache reuse correctness regression observed. High tail latency and memory growth on serving pool. Dashboard: https://internal.redwood/ops/dashboards/kv-cache. Paging @sre_oncall @dave_eng @carla_infra

emily_m (sre): I'm acknowledging. Spike started ~15:12 UTC. Tail p99 latency up 3x on a few routes, 5xxs concentrated on generation endpoints. Heap growth on some pods ~30% in 8 minutes.

sre_oncall: Any recent rollouts or config changes we should look at?

dave_eng: Yes, we rolled eng-runtime v3.4.1 canary earlier which increased continuous_batch_size from 32 to 64. Canary finished ramping to 100% at ~14:59. I see some logs that look like seq offsets being reused across requests:

```
[15:13:07] req=tx1001 model=redwood-v1 kv_slot=12 seq_offset=256
[15:13:07] req=tx1002 model=redwood-v1 kv_slot=12 seq_offset=0   <-- unexpected
[15:13:08] req=tx1003 model=redwood-v1 kv_slot=12 seq_offset=0   <-- possible reuse
```

We might be aliasing internal seq buffers instead of copying per-request.

carla_infra: Confirmed: deploy-bot shows canary started 13:30, reached 100% at 13:59 UTC. This timing aligns with the onset of errors.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-15T13:30:12Z: rollout/eng-runtime v3.4.1 -> continuous_batch_size=64. Canary->100% 13:59:01Z.

emily_m (sre): Proposed mitigations: 1) flip feature flag to disable continuous batching, 2) rollback to previous runtime version, or 3) purge KV caches for impacted tenants. Rolling back may be heavier; flag flip is fastest. Thoughts?

sre_oncall: Prioritize least-disruptive: flip the flag global-off, then run targeted KV purges for tenants reporting errors. Dave, can you prepare a code patch for the reuse behavior?

dave_eng: Yes. I have a small change to ensure seq offsets are copied into request-local storage rather than referenced. Draft here:

```
- auto seq_ptr = kv_cache->seq_offsets.get_ptr(slot);
- req.seq_view = seq_ptr; // borrowed view
+ auto seq_copy = kv_cache->seq_offsets.copy(slot);
+ req.seq_view = std::move(seq_copy); // isolated per request
```

I'm building and will canary the patch.

carla_infra: Running flag flip command now: 

```
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \n  https://api.internal/flags/continuous_batching \n  -d '{"enabled": false, "env":"prod"}'
```

carla_infra: Feature flag set to disabled. Confirming propagation across regions. :white_check_mark:

support-bot: Early impact summary: ~900 requests impacted in the window; three customers reported errors (AcmeCorp: ~280 reqs, FinTechX: ~170 reqs, EduLabs: ~80 reqs). No evidence of data leakage.

emily_m (sre): After disabling batching, we observed error rate drop to baseline within ~5 minutes and memory utilization stabilizing.

dave_eng: Hotfix build passed unit tests; pushing to canary now. Patch ensures per-request ownership of seq offset buffers.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-15T15:18:22Z: patch/kv-cache-reuse-fix -> canary SUCCESS
deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-15T15:28:10Z: patch/kv-cache-reuse-fix -> prod SUCCESS

emily_m (sre): Verified post-deploy metrics: 5xx rates back to baseline, p99 latency recovered. We'll keep continuous batching disabled until we validate with stress tests and additional safety guards.

sre_oncall: Handoff plan: I'll watch for 30 minutes then handoff to carla_infra for longer follow-up. Carla, take infra owner?

carla_infra: I'm taking post-incident infra ownership. I'll keep flag off, and schedule a controlled ramp with additional integration tests and gating.

paul_product: Customer impact: severity P1 for a subset of customers. @jason_cs can you draft outreach to affected customers (AcmeCorp & FinTechX) offering details and next steps?

jason_cs: Will draft and sync with Emily and Paul. Prioritize the two most affected.

support-bot: Metrics: mitigation window ~16 minutes (15:12 -> 15:28). Affected request proportion ~0.3% of traffic. No global SLO breach but localized customer impact.

emily_m (sre): Initial postmortem notes:
- Root cause: continuous batching ramp exposed KV cache reuse bug causing stale seq offsets and cross-request leakage.
- Immediate mitigations: feature-flag off, targeted KV purge, canary + prod hotfix deploy.
- Remediations: add unit/regression tests for KV cache lifetime semantics; add integration tests for batching size ramp behavior; implement router-side sanity checks for seq offset anomalies; add an alert correlating memory growth + p99 increases.

dave_eng: I'll own the code fixes and tests. ETA: 72 hours for comprehensive tests and a rollout-safe patch.

carla_infra: I'll own rollout policy and gating changes. ETA: 48 hours to add automated canary gating to block rapid ramp if memory/seq anomalies detected.

paul_product: I'll coordinate customer comms and schedule a cross-functional postmortem review.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS -> mitigated, monitoring. Mitigation timestamp: 15:28 UTC. Owners: carla_infra (post-incident), dave_eng (code).

emily_m (sre): Closing note: no data corruption detected, evidence points to pointer aliasing causing seq offset reuse. Recommend keeping continuous batching disabled until we've validated correctness and safe ramping. Great job triaging quickly. :thumbsup: 

sre_oncall: Thanks all. Closing incident thread; please add timeline and attachments to the postmortem doc.

jason_cs: I'll send customer outreach in 30 min.

support-bot: Post-incident tasks: create postmortem, include timeline, list impacted customers, add reproducer steps, and attach logs.

emily_m (sre): Postmortem owner: carla_infra. Target draft by 2026-03-17.

carla_infra: Acknowledged. Starting timeline reconstruction and log collection now.
